Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now, start to finish.

## Problem
The Build orchestrator on main is stale. `_claude/builds/profiles/*/orchestrator.json` is a read-only export of `_claude/builds/store.json`, regenerated after every store write. Sessions write the store on their own feature branch, so main never sees step progress until (if ever) the branch merges. Branch and PR fields are left blank. Result today: in the Urgent profile, dock-engine (done in open PR #245, branch claude/molly-fable) and token-control (done in open PRs #246 claude/token-control and #250 claude/token-control-opus) still show pending with 0 steps done, and theme-editor has an unmerged branch claude/theme-editor nobody linked. Banners and THREADS are wrong as a result.

Brett's rule: every completed step, no matter how small, must reach the orchestrator and appear on main immediately. The orchestrator must be aware every step of the way so it can update the banners and the threads.

## First (before code)
1. Register this build in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `orch-live-sync`, category Urgent, branch claude/orch-live-sync), with the steps below. Register the in-progress banner entry per the standing session rules.
2. Check the pending build queue per the standing rules.

## Steps
- s1 Lift Tooltip mode out of the Terminal plugin into the framework toolbar component (web reference + axf.css; Compose twin in PORTING.md unless trivial) as one shared behaviour; the Terminal uses the framework version (no duplicate code left in the plugin).
- s2 Device rule: double-tap confirm only when the input is touch (pointer: coarse / touch events / compact window class on a touch device). Mouse/trackpad/pen-hover = single click + hover tooltip. Decide per interaction (a touchscreen laptop: touch = double tap, mouse = single click).
- s3 Adopt everywhere: every toolbar in the console, every plugin, axHub web, AmberX (Capacitor), Molly, walkthrough-studio, templates/boilerplates, so new apps get it by default. Inventory every toolbar first and list them in the report.
- s4 Future-proof: the framework toolbar has it ON by default; a check (like check-controls) fails CI if any toolbar is built outside the framework toolbar or turns the behaviour off without an explicit, recorded reason. Add the rule to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar uses tap-to-confirm on touch (framework toolbar); single click on desktop.'
- s5 Settings > Appearance (or Interaction): on/off for touch, arm duration (default 3 s); per-toolbar override only via the setting, not code. Destructive buttons keep their own confirm on top.
- s6 Tests (touch vs mouse paths, timeout, second tap on a different button re-arms instead of running), screenshots phone + desktop, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/toolbar-tap-confirm.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): make all of this ONE Toolbars plugin
The framework toolbar becomes a **Toolbars plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall) that owns every toolbar in every app, existing and future. Everything below is part of it.

### Settings
- Plugin settings (Settings > Plugins > Toolbars): global on/off for the touch double-tap tip (default on, phone/touch only), arm duration, defaults for all toolbars (theme, colours, density, icon size, labels on/off, position).
- **Every toolbar carries its OWN settings** (stored per toolbar id, synced via axHub like other settings): theming and colours (tokens/assets only: colour theme, style, background, button style, icon/label size, spacing, rounded/flat, opacity), layout (position, orientation, wrap vs scroll vs overflow menu, show/hide, auto-hide), behaviour (double-tap override for this toolbar, tooltips), and its button list.
- **Context-menu hooks on every toolbar** (right-click / long-press): 'Toolbar settings' (that toolbar's own settings), 'Edit toolbar' (opens the Toolbar editor), 'All toolbars...' (Toolbars plugin page that lists and controls every toolbar in the app). Contributed as runtime context items, so every existing and future toolbar gets them; CI check fails any toolbar without them.

### Toolbar editor
- Opens from the toolbar context menu. Add / remove / reorder / group / separators, edit each button (label, icon, tooltip text, action/hook, colour, visibility by level/role, keyboard shortcut), reset to default, undo/redo, live preview, save as an asset so it's hot-swappable and shareable.

### Drag and drop hooks anywhere
- A **hook** = any actionable thing in the app (menu item, nav item, toolbar button, banner item, 'Go to it' hooks, plugin commands from control@1 / plugin-commands-auto, settings pages, screens). Reuse the control@1 command registry and the pending `context-menu-editor` idea (save the action/destination, not the element).
- Drag any hook from anywhere and drop it on a **drop target**: any toolbar, the navigation menu, the banners, application menus, context menus, Home. Drag a button from one toolbar to another; nav menu -> toolbar and toolbar -> nav menu.
- On drop: a **configure dialog that depends on where it's dropped** (toolbar = new button dialog; nav menu = nav item dialog; banner = banner item dialog; menu = menu item dialog), prefilled with default values from the hook (label, icon, action, tooltip), with all the options for that target. Confirm creates it; move vs copy choice (default: copy from menus, move between toolbars), undo.
- Make it a framework contract: `drop-target@1` (what it accepts + which configure dialog) and `hook@1` (draggable action descriptor), open registries so any plugin/app can add targets and hooks without kernel changes. Phone: long-press to pick up, drag with edge auto-scroll, drop zones highlight.
- **Banners:** only add the banner drop target through the generic contract. Do NOT merge or rewrite banner-pack (#251), banner-editor (#254) or banners-one work; Brett is reviewing those himself. Note any overlap in the report.
- Rules: add to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar is a Toolbars plugin toolbar: per-toolbar settings + editor via its context menu, tap-to-confirm on touch only, accepts dropped hooks.' Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.

- Settings > Menus: 'Talking about' section on/off, how long topics stay.
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'When the conversation moves to something in the console, call console_context with it.'

  - Animations: open/close (fade, scale, slide, drop, none), duration + easing, submenu reveal, item stagger, hover effect, highlight pulse for 'Talking about' items, reduced-motion respected.
  - Sections: order, on/off, max items each, labels, icons, collapse/expand, show 'why suggested' hint.
  - Behaviour: learning on/off + reset, topic lifetime, open on hover vs click (desktop), long-press time (phone), keyboard shortcuts.

- Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the Toolbars plugin (toolbar-tap-confirm build) through framework APIs - don't edit their files; share the hook@1 / drop-target@1 contract if it's on main.
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get/set menu settings, presets, reset learning, topics).

Phone + desktop. If an LLM is needed to turn the brief into a mockup spec, do it ONCE per build at launch with the cheapest capable model and cache it; record the cost on the item.
- s2 UI Review item created at launch with status 'Predicted - approve the look', badge 'Predicted', before = current real screen (from main), after = predicted mockup. Brett can Approve look / Ask changes (comment goes to the build as an addendum before it starts or at the next step) / Reject (build is held, not started).
- s3 Setting (Claude settings / UI Review settings): 'Wait for my look approval before UI builds start' (default OFF; when ON, UI-touching builds queue until the predicted look is approved).
- s4 While running, the predicted shot refreshes as the diff grows; when the build finishes, the real after-shot replaces it live (badge 'Real'), with a toggle to compare predicted vs real.
- s5 Backfill: create predicted items now for every queued/running build that touches UI (toolbar-tap-confirm, crew-live, follow-amber, claude-settings, agent-pick, home-cards-live, smart-menus).
- s6 Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (predict, list predicted, approve look). Tests, screenshots, report `_claude/builds/reports/ui-review-predicted.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
